newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Down but sentiment remain firm.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Down but sentiment remain firm.

text.p: Singapore's high sulphur fuel oil market edged down slightly on fresh offers at lower levels amid the absence of a trader who had bought several cargoes over the past few weeks, traders said.
But sentiment remains firm because most felt the trader's absence was temporary.
In late Friday trade, the 180-cst grade was offered down to $99 per tonne from $101 heard earlier, in line with overnight falls in crude values, traders said.
The 380-cst was offered at $96.5 but buying interest in both grades was low, they said.
The Singapore trader has been consistently buying since late June, with the latest 180-cst cargo bought at $100 per tonne for early August delivery on Thursday.
"He is buying to supply Vietnam, Indonesia and China. The demand is quite stable but not very big," said one trader.

Traders said prices for the 180-cst grade cargoes should hover around the $100-per-tonne level in the near term with moderate support from the local trader, who has along with its sister company bought more than 10 cargoes in the past month.
The SIMEX fuel oil futures contract market was quiet with no transaction reported late on Friday. The August contract was bid/offered at $98/$99 and the July contract was at $97.5/$99.0.
Fuel oil swaps slid slightly also amid falls in crude values, with July swaps down to $98.75/$99.50 from Thursday's $99.50/$100.25. August swaps were at $98.50/$99.00 against $98.75/$99.25.
In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, sentiment remained strong due to tight supplies in July.
Supplies from Indonesia stood at 2.6 million barrels in July, compared with 3.6 million in June, due to refinery maintenance turnaround there.
"The $16-per-barrel level should be a solid floor for the market for the rest of this month," said one trader.
